title: A spiritual friend
hookLine: the Buddha called good friendship the whole of the holy life (Samyutta Nikaya 45.2)
tomorrow: a town full of rival teachers. how do you pick one?

cards: Plenty of closets hold a sweatshirt that used to be someone else's. Too big, a little faded, and still the first thing grabbed on a bad day. Friends leave things in our hands.
Ananda, the monk who attended the Buddha, had been thinking about friends.
One day he came to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said what he'd worked out: half of the holy life, venerable sir, is good friendship.

teach.b: It sounds generous. Half! The Buddha's answer, in the Samyutta Nikaya: not so, Ananda.

teach.h: THE WHOLE OF THE HOLY LIFE.
teach.b: Good friendship, good companionship, is the whole of the holy life.
A monk who has a good friend can be expected to walk the whole noble eightfold path. Then he points to himself.
Beings who are bound to be born, to grow old, to die, are set free, he says, by taking him as their good friend. The Pali word is kalyana mitta. Kalyana: good, lovely.
Mitta: friend. So the teaching, in this sutta: the friend isn't a nice extra beside the real practice.

teach.h: THE BUDDHA AS THE GOOD FRIEND.
teach.b: With a good friend, the Buddha says, a monk can be expected to walk the whole path. That's why the Buddha can call himself the good friend. So a spiritual friend isn't just someone who agrees with you.
In the sutta, it's someone whose company keeps you walking the path. Like the borrowed sweatshirt: something of them stays with you on the bad days. Ananda thought it was half.
The Buddha said it was the whole of it.

how: Buddhists speak of the kalyana mitta, the good friend on the path: a teacher, a fellow practitioner, the community. Some people name one spiritual friend whose company helps them keep going.

o: a good friend whose company helps you on the path
a lucky charm that keeps away bad karma
a monk who lives alone and teaches by letter

games.q: the whole of it: tap the pairs.
p: not so: it is the whole

s: the Buddha agreed that good friendship is half of the holy life
he corrected Ananda: not so. It is the whole of the holy life.
in this sutta, the Buddha calls himself a good friend to beings
beings bound to birth, aging and death are freed by taking him as their good friend.
a spiritual friend is someone who always agrees with you
the good friend is the one whose company makes the path easier to walk.

games.q: you're choosing between a fun friend who never talks about anything deep, and a quieter one who helps you keep going. which is the kalyana mitta?
o: the one whose company makes the path easier to walk.
the fun one, because a spiritual friend should keep things light.
neither; the Buddha said the path is walked alone.
games.why: In Samyutta Nikaya 45.2, the Buddha calls good friendship the whole of the holy life: the path is walked with others.

practice: Hold something a friend gave you, if it's near: a mug, a note, a bracelet, a book. Feel its weight, its edges, how warm or cool it is in your hands. For the rest of the sit, let that friend's name rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: Kalyana mitta: Pali for a good friend on the path, the friend the Buddha called the whole of the holy life.

orig.note: Pali, from the Buddhist suttas: kalyana, good or lovely; mitta, friend.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole of it. Not half, Ananda, the Buddha said: the whole. Day 1656, done.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2 (Upaddha Sutta: half of the holy life; not so, Ananda; the whole of the holy life; the Buddha as good friend)
